jurisdiction.name: Côte d’Ivoire
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Côte d'Ivoire steers AI through its National AI Strategy (SNIA 2030) and National Data Governance Strategy (SNGD 2030), both dated 2024 and officially handed to the Prime Minister on 13 March 2025, with the 2013 personal data protection law as its only binding text. An announced AI bill, a national AI agency, the AI pillar of the 2026-2028 digital roadmap and a national AI alliance pact signed in September 2026 have no published texts.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Digital Transition and Digitalisation
narrative.review_notes: This review was first completed on 12 October 2026, redone in a longer pass on 13 October 2026 and rechecked on 22 October 2026, covering Parliament, the government, each ministry and each sector regulator. On 22 October 2026 the official sites were checked through web search only, and no new official AI text was found. Not yet verified from the official text: any AI material in the Official Journal or from the cyber agency, the finance and labour ministries and the competition and higher-education quality bodies. The AI bill, the national AI agency, the roadmap's AI pillar and the AI alliance pact are tracked as leads.

instruments.official_title: Stratégie Nationale de l'Intelligence Artificielle à l'horizon 2030 (SNIA 2030)
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministère de la Transition Numérique et de la Digitalisation (Ministry of Digital Transition and Digitalisation)
instruments.current_status: Published on the ministry's strategies page (a copy is also hosted on anssi.gouv.ci). The document itself is dated only 2024. The government portal gouv.ci reports that on Thursday 13 March 2025, at the Sofitel Hôtel Ivoire in Abidjan, the Minister of Digital Transition officially handed the SNIA and SNGD documents to the Prime Minister. The notice does not describe a formal government adoption, and no Council of Ministers adoption act was found. The National AI Agency (ANIA) and Council (CNIA) it proposes had no founding text by October 2026 (see leads). In September 2026 the ministry said a 2026-2028 digital roadmap with an AI pillar and a State-private sector national AI alliance pact build on the strategy; neither text is published (see leads).
instruments.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's first national AI strategy, with a vision of making inclusive, ethical and responsible AI an accelerator of transformation by 2030, built on three pillars: investment, inclusion and governance. The investment pillar includes an axis on drafting a regulatory and ethical framework (stronger personal-data law aligned with international standards, a supervisory entity for AI data, algorithmic audits for critical sectors such as health, education and public administration, and transparency obligations on developers). The governance pillar provides for a National AI Agency (ANIA) housing a National AI Council (CNIA) to steer, coordinate and monitor implementation.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Central AI policy document; sets the plan for an AI regulatory framework and a national AI agency and council.
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Digital Transition and Technological Innovation
metadata_gaps: publication_date: the document states only the year 2024; the official handover to the Prime Minister on 2025-03-13 is stated on gouv.ci, but no adoption act was found
instruments.evidence_reference: Re-checked 2026-10-13. curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): 71-page PDF (HTTP 200, application/pdf, 1.69 MB) downloaded from the ministry's Publications > Planification > Stratégies page and read with pdftotext; it states only 'Côte d'Ivoire 2024'. WebFetch of the same PDF URL also returned the file (HTTP 200, binary). Handover date read via WebFetch from the gouv.ci news notice (curl to gouv.ci was reset).

instruments.official_title: Stratégie Nationale de la Gouvernance des Données à l'horizon 2030 (SNGD 2030)
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministère de la Transition Numérique et de la Digitalisation (Ministry of Digital Transition and Digitalisation)
instruments.current_status: Published on the ministry's strategies page alongside the SNIA 2030. The document is dated only 2024, with a 2024-2030 period. The government portal gouv.ci reports that the minister officially handed it to the Prime Minister together with the SNIA on 13 March 2025 in Abidjan. No government adoption act was found.
instruments.summary: Companion strategy to the SNIA 2030 setting national data governance for 2024-2030 around six strategic pillars: culture and ethics, infrastructure, interoperability and accessibility, quality data, innovation, and skills. Among its objectives is creating the framework for secure AI development, and it proposes a strong public-sector data governance body, ideally attached to the Prime Minister's office, that would combine data governance and AI development outside the field of regulation. It includes actions on AI-based data processing, a supercomputer for data and AI, and AI and big-data R&D.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Data-governance foundation for AI; proposes a combined data and AI governance body.
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Digital Transition and Technological Innovation
metadata_gaps: publication_date: the document states only the year 2024; official handover on 2025-03-13 (gouv.ci), no adoption act found
instruments.evidence_reference: Re-checked 2026-10-13. curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): 61-page PDF (HTTP 200, application/pdf, 8.1 MB) downloaded and read with pdftotext; it states only 'Côte d'Ivoire 2024' and the period 2024-2030. instruments.official_title: Loi n° 2013-450 du 19 juin 2013 relative à la protection des données à caractère personnel
instruments.english_title: Law No. 2013-450 of 19 June 2013 on the Protection of Personal Data
instruments.issuing_authority: Assemblée nationale; promulgated by the President of the Republic
instruments.current_status: In force. Dated 19 June 2013 and published in the Journal officiel of 8 August 2013 (JORCI p. 474). The SNIA 2030 calls for it to be strengthened and aligned with international standards. No amending law or bill was found on official sites (ARTCI, digital ministry, Assemblée nationale) by 13 October 2026.
instruments.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's personal data protection law, applying to public and private controllers and making the authority in charge of personal data protection (ARTCI) responsible for declarations, authorisations and supervision of processing. It sets core principles (consent and other legal bases, purpose limitation, accuracy, transparency, security, confidentiality) and special rules for sensitive data. Article 25 prohibits any court decision involving an assessment of a person's behaviour from being based on automated processing of personal data intended to evaluate aspects of their personality.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General data protection law governing AI training and use on personal data; contains an automated-processing rule (art. 25).
metadata_gaps: effective_date: the law states no separate entry-into-force date (art. 54: published in the Journal officiel and executed as a law of the State; art. 53 gives existing controllers six months from entry into force to comply)
instruments.evidence_reference: Re-checked 2026-10-13. curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): the Journal officiel scan of 8 August 2013 (HTTP 200, application/pdf, 6.2 MB) was downloaded again from ARTCI's Textes juridiques > Lois page. WebFetch of the ARTCI Lois page confirmed the title and the download link. The text was read in full in the first pass (image-only scan, articles 1-25 and 49-54).

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Official law listings, Parliament, the government and the digital ministry, and each ministry and sector regulator were searched at national level. No qualifying AI-governance document was found for risk and assurance, procurement, cybersecurity, transparency, standards, sandboxes, readiness indices, sector rules, generative AI, drafts and consultations, international agreements, or past instruments. The Official Journal's full-text search requires a login, so it and several ministry and regulator sites remain to be checked, and the AI bill announced in 2025 and other reported items are listed under Leads.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: thin pass 2026-10-13 (second, longer deep review: up to 45 minutes, one agent, national level only, PROTOCOL §6; every existing record re-checked; each ministry and sector regulator searched one by one). Thin pass 2026-10-13: 3 existing records re-checked with curl and WebFetch; SNIA and SNGD current_status updated with the official handover to the Prime Minister (13 Mar 2025, gouv.ci notice; no adoption act found; publication_date stays 2024); Law 2013-450 JO scan reachable again, no amendment. sgg.gouv.ci Journal officiel needs login (no gazette search). Not reached: ANSSI (TLS/503), finances.gouv.ci, emploi.gouv.ci (403), concurrence.ci, anaq-sup.ci, crepmf.org, ARTCI LINP AI paper (404), CoE treaty page (403). CODINORM: no ISO/IEC 42001/23894/22989 adoption. BCEAO, CREPMF, CIMA regional. SNDECI 2024-2028 AI in passing (lead). Convention 108: not a party. Units covered: Law: Journal officiel (sgg.gouv.ci): full-text search is not public (login and download code required), so no gazette search was possible. Law listings on the digital ministry and ARTCI sites were re-checked (2013-450, 2013-451 cybercrime, 2013-546 e-transactions, 2017-803 information society, 2023-901 startups, 2024-352 electronic communications, decrees 2013-302, 2014-729, 2015-80): none found to contain AI-specific provisions beyond art. 25 of 2013-450. Ordinance 2024-950 (e-administration exchanges, ratified April 2025) has no AI content according to the ministry notice. No deepfake or AI offence and no data-protection amendment were found. Law 2013-450 was re-checked (kept).; Parliament: assnat.ci: the law listings (mostly up to 2019) and 2026 session news were checked. No AI bill, data protection bill or deepfake bill has been tabled. The 2nd ordinary session of 2026 (opened 1 October 2026) lists AI only as an internal modernisation and MP-training topic (lead). The AI bill announced in 2025 remains a lead.; Government: Digital ministry (MTNIT): strategies page re-checked (SNIA 2030 and SNGD 2030 kept; SNNCI 2021-2025 evaluation, innovation strategy and cybersecurity strategy 2021-2025 have no AI pillar). Reports, orientation, decree and ordinance pages were checked, and 2025-2026 news on AI was scanned. Found: an official handover date of 13 March 2025 for both strategies (gouv.ci), and leads for the national AI alliance pact (11 Sep 2026), the 2026-2028 digital roadmap AI pillar, the Mistral partnership and the JDN 2026 recommendations. Council of Ministers communiqués on gouv.ci/sgg.gouv.ci: no AI decree or bill (the Feb 2026 PADCI loan ratification is already a lead). ANSUT: AI event news only.; Ministries: Education (MENA): SNDECI 2024-2028 digital education strategy mentions AI only in passing (lead), and no AI charter or guidance was found. Higher education (MESRS): AI promotion events only, no AI guidance. Health: no AI document (only a clinical research training item). Justice: no AI directive found. Defence: SIADE AI/defence fair only, no AI doctrine. Finance/tax (finances.gouv.ci unreachable; DGI): nothing. Labour/employment (emploi.gouv.ci 403): nothing found via web search. Interior/security: nothing. Agriculture: speeches on AI only. Foreign affairs: Paris AI Action Summit declaration signature (international, Feb 2025), no national document. Several ministry sites are script-rendered and were searched through web search with domain filters.; Regulators: ARTCI (telecoms and data protection authority): site search and Décisions page show only AI event news, plus authorisation decisions with no AI-specific content (e.g. video-surveillance). A reported LINP AI paper returned 404 (lead). BCEAO, CREPMF (unreachable) and CIMA/CRCA are regional bodies, and BCEAO and CIMA site searches returned no AI rules. HACA (audiovisual regulator): hosts RIARC/REFRAM network AI principles and a declaration, which are not national (lead). AIRP (pharmaceutical regulator): no AI content. Higher-education quality agency (ANAQ-Sup): site unreachable, nothing found. Competition commission: site unreachable, nothing found. ANSSI (cyber agency): TLS/503 errors on both methods; web search found only a hosted SNIA copy, no AI security guidance. CODINORM (standards): no national adoption of ISO/IEC 42001/23894/22989 found. ARCOP (public procurement regulator): site search returned no AI content.; Convention 108: Côte d'Ivoire is not a party: no accession act or law authorising ratification was found on assnat.ci or the digital ministry and ARTCI sites, and the Council of Europe treaty page was not reachable (403). Set to null.. Not reached: Journal officiel full text (sgg.gouv.ci: login and download code required); ANSSI site (anssi.gouv.ci: certificate error with curl, HTTP 503 with WebFetch); finances.gouv.ci, emploi.gouv.ci (403), concurrence.ci, anaq-sup.ci, crepmf.org: unreachable; covered only through web search; ARTCI LINP AI paper (404); Council of Europe treaty office page (403). Could not verify: Journal officiel full-text search (gated) - no gazette check for AI terms was possible; Government adoption act for SNIA/SNGD: none found; only the 13 March 2025 handover is stated officially; ARTCI LINP AI paper (404); ANSSI documents page (unreachable). risk-assurance, procurement, cyber-security, transparency, standards, sandbox, index-readiness, sectoral, generative-ai, drafts, international, historical: no material found.
Wording note 2026-10-19 (narrative.review_notes): The Official Journal requires a login, and the cyber agency's, finance and labour ministries' and the competition and higher-education quality bodies' websites could not be accessed.
Wording note 2026-10-19 (coverage_audit.no_material_found_note): The Official Journal's full-text search requires a login and several ministry and regulator sites were unavailable, so these remain to be checked,
Wave 4 recheck 2026-10-22 (one agent, web search and WebFetch only): the session's egress proxy answered 403 to every curl CONNECT, so no official site was opened directly by curl; WebFetch of telecom.gouv.ci and artci.ci URLs was refused for lack of a search provenance. 14 web searches (FR/EN) across gouv.ci, sgg.gouv.ci, telecom.gouv.ci, artci.ci, anssi.gouv.ci, assnat.ci and ministries returned only press coverage (IMPACT IA 2026 pact of 11 Sep 2026, Mistral partnership, roadmap) and the gouv.ci press digest of 12 Dec 2025 (no AI instrument). No new record; all leads kept.

leads.note: Signed in Abidjan on 11 September 2026 at the close of IMPACT IA 2026, according to the ministry's own news page (telecom.gouv.ci/new/index.php/actualite/194). It sets a State-private sector framework for cooperation, data access, infrastructure, skills, research and an ethical and responsible framework for AI use. The pact text is not published on official sites. 2026-10-22: the pact text is still not published; press reports on the 11 September 2026 signing name no document.

Press reports say the AI pillar includes an ethical-use framework. No roadmap document is published on official sites; the 2026 budget presentation 'Les grands axes de priorités' (March 2026) only mentions implementing the AI strategy. 2026-10-22: no roadmap document found on official sites.

leads.title: Intégration de l'intelligence artificielle dans les travaux de l'Assemblée nationale
leads.english_title: Use of AI in the work of the National Assembly
leads.note: Assemblée nationale news on the opening of the 2nd 2026 ordinary session (assnat.ci) states that AI should support but never replace human judgement, and announces MP training from 12 October 2026 with the digital ministry. This is an internal institutional plan with no adopted rules, so it fails the scope test.
